rows.value: 5 seeds. (a) psi construction: N_CTX=96 contexts x up to 30 DISJOINT slot groups per n, drawn from one randperm of a pool of 8192 unit gestalts whose psi_hat is precomputed at that context. Disjoint, so no within-group duplicate can manufacture a tie. (b) normal yardstick: 40000 exact iid N(0,1) draws per n. Both z-score with std(unbiased=False), i.e. rsr.py:369 verbatim, and take the gap between the two SMALLEST z-scores -- the quantity the argmin turns on, same definition as EvictionRecord.score_margin (rsr.py:406). n sweep = [4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64].

rows.value: For each M in [8, 16, 40]: 12 streams x S=80 steps, b-free learned-head driver. `lifetime` = age at eviction = t - written_at[victim], over EVICTED slots only (slots alive at stream end are censored and excluded -- stated, not hidden). The FIFO column is a REAL `FIFOPolicy` driving its OWN memory over the same context stream -- not a statistic read out of the learned driver's memory, which would be a different policy's contents. The oldest-live-slot column IS read out of the learned driver's memory and is labelled as such.

rows.value: For each M in [8, 16, 40], at S=80: a driver arm (b_enabled=False, nu=0) owns the memory so the MemoryState sequence is IDENTICAL across arms; every arm shares ONE BilinearValueHead so psi_hat is bit-identical; 12 streams/seed, 5 seeds. A 'flip' is an eviction where the b-enabled arm's victim differs from the b-free driver's on the same state. Arms: ['formula_M', 'formula_realized', 'fixed_0.1']. EMA half-life is E[lifetime]/4 with the SAME E[lifetime] that set that arm's gamma_b (correction 4's own pairing).

verdict.falsifier: a single FROZEN b_max gives `b` comparable strength at every M the project trains (M = 8 for the D-5 / correction 6 E7 model, M = 16 for synthetic, M = 40 for corpora / PG-19).
verdict.detail: ORDER STATISTIC. b_max / median-top-2-z-margin is 1.8877 +/- 0.0500 at M = 8, 2.5924 +/- 0.0526 at M = 16 and 3.1749 +/- 0.0820 at M = 40 -- a swing of 1.6824 +/- 0.0486 across exactly the two M the project trains. Exact-normal yardstick: 1.9261 / 2.5359 / 3.1905. The brief's predicted ~1.67 swing is confirmed. b is MECHANICALLY STRONGER per unit of b at larger M, because the gap between the two smallest of n z-scores shrinks with n while b_max does not move. REALIZED FLIPS. Under correction 4's own formula fed the FIFO lifetime E[lifetime] = M -- gamma_b = 4/M, i.e. 0.5 / 0.25 / 0.1 -- b changes 0.4671 +/- 0.0170 of victims at M = 8, 0.5336 +/- 0.0215 at M = 16 and 0.5950 +/- 0.0129 at M = 40. The formula's 1/M scaling OVER-CORRECTS relative to the order statistic: the arm with gamma_b HELD at the M = 40 value (0.1) gives 0.3227 / 0.4854 / 0.5950, so with gamma_b fixed b is weakest at small M and the formula's M-dependence is what pulls the small-M rate up. Either way the three rates are NOT comparable, and the two parameterizations of E[lifetime] are themselves far apart: realized mean slot lifetime under the learned-head driver is 7.377 / 13.317 / 26.236 against the FIFO 8 / 16 / 40. `phi` is UNTRAINED and `u_bar` is SYNTHETIC; part 1 depends on neither beyond the head's linear-functional form, part 3 depends on both.
